paper_metadata.title: Higher-Order Portfolio Optimization with Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm

summary: The paper introduces a higher-order portfolio optimization formulation with skewness and kurtosis, benchmarked on 100 DJIA-based instances spanning 6 to 15 qubits. It reports an average QAOA enhancement factor of 14.43x over uniform random sampling, but classical baselines remain strong: the constrained classical baseline achieves 74% feasibility versus 19% for QAOA, while the exact solver reaches 100% feasibility and 53% on the high-objective metric in the table shown.

experiments.description: QAOA benchmark for higher-order portfolio optimization (HUBO) with integer asset quantities, capital-based budget constraint, and higher moments (skewness/kurtosis) on 100 randomly generated DJIA-based instances.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA for higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO)
algorithm.ansatz: standard QAOA with x-mixer and cost Hamiltonian evolution
algorithm.optimizer: CMA-ES (primary reported optimizer for QAOA subroutine); also benchmarked Powell, SLSQP, COBYLA, Nelder-Mead, and L-BFGS-B
algorithm.convergence_criteria: limited number of iterations / optimizer termination; exact stopping rule not specified
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial parameter values not specified; QAOA parameters optimized classically

optimizer_settings.max_iterations: limited number of iterations (exact value not reported)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: integer asset quantities z_i encoded into binary variables with logarithmic overhead; each integer variable z in range 0..N mapped to binary bits using standard binary/logarithmic encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_z q2 K(z) - q1 S(z) + q0 z^T c z - mu^T z + lambda (z^T p^tau - C)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: budget constraint encoded as quadratic penalty term; paper also discusses an alternative binary budget encoding but uses the symmetric penalty formulation in experiments
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_{S subset I} alpha_S prod_{i in S} Z_i, with terms up to 4-body interactions from cokurtosis; budget penalty added to cost Hamiltonian

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over randomly sampled DJIA stocks with higher moments, integer quantities, and capital budget
problem_instance.dataset_name: Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) / yfinance stock data

dataset_specification.preprocessing: geometric mean annualized with frequency 252 for expected returns; covariance annualized with frequency 252; coskewness and cokurtosis computed from returns; random sampling of 2-10 companies; random budget up to 6000; instances with >15 qubits excluded

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: returns computed from closing prices; geometric mean used for mean returns; arithmetic mean with f=1 used in covariance formula; higher moments computed from normalized central moments; instances filtered to fit 15-qubit simulator
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 random instances; compared QAOA against exact eigensolver and classical continuous-variable baselines; results reported across qubit counts 6-15; multiple optimizer comparisons for QAOA subroutine

hardware.framework: Qiskit and PennyLane (both mentioned as frameworks that can construct the QAOA circuit; implementation available on GitHub)

implementation_details.classical_solver: SciPy SLSQP for continuous baseline; CVXPY for integer-programming discretization; exact eigensolver / sparse eigensolver for small instances; CMA-ES and other classical optimizers for QAOA subroutine
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: continuous-variable portfolio optimization solved first, then discretized via integer programming baseline; QAOA instances generated from same data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: min-max normalization of objective values across methods; budget utilization computed; discrete allocations compared

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: not reported in numeric form; figure shows optimizer comparison and average objective values

results.unit: x enhancement over uniform random probability
x enhancement over uniform random probability (worst observed)

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports empirical performance comparisons and QAOA enhancement factors, but no asymptotic or wall-clock speedup claim is demonstrated.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; experiments are simulator-based on 6-15 qubits and no asymptotic crossover analysis is provided
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a scalable fault-tolerant implementation of QAOA for higher-order portfolio optimization plus efficient encoding of integer variables and budget constraints; the paper does not provide resource estimates for a practical advantage regime
limiting_factors: Only simulator-sized instances up to 15 qubits
Classical baseline is competitive and often better on the reported metrics
Optimization landscape is rugged with many local minima
No proven speedup or crossover analysis

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper states the problems were sized to fit a 15-qubit simulator and does not name a real QPU.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only gate-count/depth comparison figure is mentioned without numeric values in the text provided.
Speedup order is none_proven because the paper discusses performance empirically but does not claim an asymptotic quantum speedup.
The paper reports QAOA on 100 simulator-sized portfolio instances and compares against classical baselines, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.

The authors state the HUBO formulation can encode better portfolios than classical solutions in some cases, yet also note QAOA only matched a small subset of exact/classical results and that current hardware is likely too demanding.
